tools.name: web3forms_list_forms
tools.description: List all Web3Forms forms in the account: form_id, form_name, created_at and total_count of submissions. Good first call to find a form_id. API: GET /forms.

tools.name: web3forms_list_submissions
tools.description: List submissions of one form, newest first, with fields, submitter IP address, user agent, site_url and attachments. Returns has_more and next_cursor: pass next_cursor as cursor to get the next page. API: GET /submissions.

tools.name: web3forms_get_submission
tools.description: Get one submission by id (for example sub_a1b2c3d4e5f6), with its fields, IP address, user agent, site_url and attachments. API: GET /submissions/{id}.

tools.name: web3forms_create_submission
tools.description: WRITE: create a submission on a form you own, as if a visitor sent it. It is stored, counts toward the monthly quota, and sends the notification email, autoresponder and integrations. Needs a key with the 'Create submissions' permission. There is NO idempotency key: if a call times out, check web3fo

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: web3forms_create_submission · Public sink: web3forms_create_submission.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: web3forms_create_submission · Public sink: web3forms_create_submission

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
